gap: No result ChatGPT got states how much faster the Thunderbolt link is than the NAS's own 10GbE port: on the same box, Thunderbolt reads were 1.39× faster on the DXP480T Plus, 2.13× on the TBS-h574TX and 1.70× on the TS-h966TX. UGREEN's own HDD figure (4-drive RAID 5 at 600–700 MB/s) is below the 1.09 GB/s Liliputing measured over 10GbE, so on hard drives the Thunderbolt cable mainly saves you a switch or a Mac 10GbE adapter and should not add speed.
standout_why: I compared against the cited QNAP US pages for the TVS-h674T and TVS-h874T, which give only the 20 Gbps 'maximum bandwidth' and no Thunderbolt MB/s (the h874T page gives only 590/591 MB/s over 2× 2.5GbE). I also checked QNAP's Thunderbolt 4 store page, which lists prices only, and UGREEN's 'How to Connect UGREEN NAS via Thunderbolt 4' blog, which gives HDD and SSD ranges but no Thunderbolt-vs-10GbE comparison. Both UGREEN Knowledge Center articles (607, 609) render empty when fetched. None of them puts Thunderbolt and 10GbE throughput side by side for one box, and none gives a per-bay price. QNAP's TS-h966TX page does have both numbers, but it was not among ChatGPT's results; ChatGPT only showed that model as a product card.
decides: It splits the pick by storage type. With all-flash storage, Thunderbolt is worth paying for: 1.4–2.1× the box's own 10GbE port. The TS-h966TX ($1,299, 9 bays, 2,004 MB/s read to an M4 Pro Mac in QNAP Labs) and the DXP480T Plus ($849.99, 1.51 GB/s in a copy test) give the most measured Thunderbolt speed per dollar. With hard drives, the DXP6800 Pro ($183/bay) and DXP8800 Plus ($171/bay) already have 2× 10GbE, so Thunderbolt there only saves cabling. The QNAP TVS-h674T ($417/bay) and TVS-h874T ($386/bay) are the exception: their built-in LAN is only 2× 2.5GbE (590 MB/s measured), so Thunderbolt is their only fast link without buying a card. That weakens ChatGPT's repeated 'safest pick' call for the TVS-h674T on value.

findings.label: Thunderbolt vs own 10GbE, same 100 GB copy (Liliputing)
findings.value: 1.39× faster reading from the NAS (1.51 vs 1.09 GB/s); 1.23× writing (1.42 vs 1.15 GB/s); 100 GB in 66 s vs 92 s
findings.source_title: UGREEN NASync DXP480T Plus Review: A speedy NAS with 10 GbE networking and four M.2 SSD slots - Liliputing
findings.note: Client was a NUC 13 Extreme (Windows), not a Mac. 1.51/1.09=1.39; 1.42/1.15=1.23; 100/1.51=66 s, 100/1.09=92 s. The same review measured 2,136–2,464 MB/s sequential reads over Thunderbolt SMB in CrystalDiskMark.

findings.label: Thunderbolt (Mac) vs own 10GbE (StorageReview)
findings.value: 1.84× faster writing (1,929 vs 1,050 MB/s); 2.13× faster reading (1,850 vs 868 MB/s); 100 GB read in 54 s vs 115 s
findings.source_title: QNAP TBS-h574TX Thunderbolt 4 NAS Review - StorageReview (Vince Carnevale, 2024-04-02)
findings.note: Thunderbolt was measured with ATTO on an M1 Max MacBook Pro, 10GbE with Blackmagic Disk Speed Test, so the tools differ. Volume: 5× 3.84 TB SK hynix PE8110 E1.S in RAID 5. 1929/1050=1.84; 1850/868=2.13; 100,000/1,850=54 s; 100,000/868=115 s. Windows 11 over Thunderbolt managed only 1,182 write / 1,015 read MB/s.

findings.label: Thunderbolt (Mac) vs own 10GbE (QNAP Labs)
findings.value: 1.91× faster writing (2,252 vs 1,182 MB/s); 1.70× faster reading (2,004 vs 1,181 MB/s); Thunderbolt write = 90% of the 20 Gbps (2,500 MB/s) link
findings.note: QNAP's own test: TS-h966TX-16G, 4× Samsung PM9A3 1.96 TB U.2 in RAID 5, MacBook Pro M4 Pro on macOS 26.0. Thunderbolt was measured with AJA (5K RED, 16 GB); 10GbE with SMB 1M sequential. 2252/1182=1.91; 2004/1181=1.70; 2252/2500=0.90. The flash speed applies to the 4 U.2 slots; the other 5 bays are 3.5-inch SATA.

findings.label: 4-HDD RAID 5 throughput as a share of what 10GbE already carries
findings.value: 600–700 MB/s per UGREEN, at most 0.64× the 1.09 GB/s Liliputing measured over 10GbE
findings.source_title: How to Connect UGREEN NAS via Thunderbolt 4 - UGREEN
findings.note: UGREEN gives practical reference ranges, not guarantees: single NAS HDD about 200–260 MB/s, four-drive HDD RAID 5 about 600–700 MB/s. 700/1,090=0.64, so an HDD pool does not fill 10GbE, and Thunderbolt adds no speed over the DXP6800 Pro's or DXP8800 Plus's built-in 10GbE. UGREEN lists DXP480T Plus, DXP6800 Pro and DXP8800 Plus as Thunderbolt-direct models, on UGOS 1.2.0.2121 or later.

findings.label: Built-in network ceiling without a card
findings.value: 590 MB/s write / 591 MB/s read over 2× 2.5GbE; the 20 Gbps Thunderbolt link (2,500 MB/s raw) is 4.2× that
findings.note: QNAP test: 8× Samsung 860 EVO in RAID 5, IOmeter SMB 1M, Windows Server client. 2,500/590=4.2. This is a rated cap against a measured figure, not a measured-vs-measured comparison. QNAP gives no measured Thunderbolt MB/s for the h674T or h874T. The h674T page also lists 2× 2.5GbE built in and 10/25GbE by PCIe card.
